author: Amr
subject: fix(i18n): normalise generated prose so translation runs keep CI green (#342)
body:
scripts/translate.rb writes whatever the provider returns, and a provider is
free to soft-wrap a translated paragraph across several lines — no prompt
instruction reliably prevents that. Wrapped prose landed in fr/**, turned
markdown-oneline.yml red on the translation PR, and stayed red on main once
it merged. Two committed translations were in exactly that state, so the
check is currently failing on main.

Fixed at the source rather than by excluding fr/** from the check:

- translate.rb normalises every page it writes through tools/unwrap-prose.py.
  That tool is what CI runs, so shelling out to it keeps one source of truth
  for the rule instead of a Ruby reimplementation free to drift from the
  Python classifier. Best-effort — a missing python3 warns rather than
  failing an otherwise good translation run.

- translate.yml runs the same tool as a guaranteed backstop immediately
  before the files are committed, on a runner where python3 always exists,
  then --checks its own work. Without that second call a silent failure would
  just relocate the breakage to the PR's own CI run.

- The tool is resolved relative to translate.rb via __dir__, not --root.
  --root points at the content tree being translated, which is a different
  thing and is a throwaway sandbox under test; the previous lookup silently
  skipped normalisation whenever the two differed. Caught by the new test.

- Unwrapped the two affected files so oneline passes on main again.

Regression test in test/test…

Each example is a complete Jekyll site with its own _config.yml, Gemfile,

- a full editorial light-mode restyle done entirely through
  assets/css/user-overrides.css — no theme files modified

Information architecture is modelled on swerveofshore.com; all content,
branding, and artwork are original demo material written for this repo.

Also fixes an exclude-list drift: _config_dev.yml redefines `exclude:`

author: Amr
subject: fix(i18n): exclude admin config page from translation to unbreak Pages deploy (#349)
body:
The GitHub Pages production build failed rendering the generated
fr/about/settings/config.md with:

  Could not locate the included file '_config.yml' in any of
  ["/github/workspace/fr/about/settings"] ... in fr/about/settings/config.md

The English admin utility pages/_about/settings/config.md embeds a raw
_config.yml dump via `{% include_relative _config.yml %}`. The translation
pipeline copied the page into the fr/ tree without its sibling _config.yml
data file, so the include could not resolve and the whole production build
died.

Exclude the page from translation (it is an admin config dashboard with no
prose to translate), remove the stale generated fr/about/settings/config.md
and its _data/i18n/manifest.yml entry, and refresh the raw-wrapped config
mirror to satisfy the config-mirror drift check.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

author: Amr
subject: feat(ci): deploy the site via Actions so examples reach the live domain (#353)
body:
The example site added in #339 was never reachable at zer0-mistakes.com, and
nothing linked to it. Both follow from the same cause.

zer0-mistakes.com is built by GitHub's classic "deploy from a branch" Pages
builder: one `jekyll build` with _config.yml. examples/ sits in that config's
`exclude:` list, so nothing under it is ever emitted. It cannot simply be
un-excluded either — each example is a SEPARATE Jekyll site with its own
_config.yml, its own `series` collection, and its own skin. Folded into the
main build its collection would not be declared and its entries would not
render at all.

One classic build cannot produce two differently-configured sites, so this
moves deployment to Actions and runs one build per site:

  _site/                           theme site      (_config.yml)
  _site/examples/swerve-of-shore/  the example     (+ _config_deploy.yml)

Adding a second example means adding it to the `example` loop.

New examples/swerve-of-shore/_config_deploy.yml points the example at the
live domain and its subpath, and resolves the theme to this repository's
sources rather than the published gem — so the demo shows the theme as it is
on main, not as it was at the last release.

Nav entry added under Docs, as an absolute path: the target is not in
site.html_pages (examples/ is excluded from this site's build), so the
theme's usual existence-guard pattern does not apply here.

The build job verifies the stitched tree before upload — theme index, each
example index, and…

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): unbreak the production Pages build, frozen since 2026-08-05 (#356)
body:
zer0-mistakes.com has not published anything since #346. The Actions deploy
added in #353 surfaced it loudly on its first run; the classic builder had been
failing the same way, silently, for two days. /fr/ 404s live while fr/** is not
excluded — that mismatch is the tell.

Three independent faults, each fatal to the whole build. Jekyll aborts on the
first, so each one was hidden behind the last:

1. _layouts/collection.html sorted site[page.collection] unguarded. A page can
   select this layout in front matter while living outside any collection,
   making the lookup nil; Liquid's sort then raises "Cannot sort a null object."
   and takes down the ENTIRE build, not just that page. Now falls back to an
   empty list. Verified non-behavioural: /docs/ renders 92 cards before and
   after, matching the live page exactly.

2. scripts/translate.rb copied `layout: collection` into the flat fr/** tree,
   which is precisely the misconfiguration above — fr/docs/index.md was the page
   that killed the site. Collection-only layouts are now dropped so the
   `path: fr` default (layout: default) applies; the affected page is
   regenerated. Covered by a new test that fails without the fix.

3. CHANGELOG.md is a published page (/CHANGELOG/ is live), so its prose is
   parsed as Liquid. Two entries quoted Liquid tags without a raw guard. One
   genuinely executed include_relative on _config.yml, which then tripped over a
   literal mermaid tag inside a config comment — jekyll-mermaid is …

subject: feat(docs): theme-canary reporting contract for downstream theme-scouts (FF-0019) (#358)
body:
Publish the canonical upstream bug-intake protocol that consumer
theme-scout agents (it-journey, lifehacker.dev) must follow when filing
theme defects here, replacing two private divergent conventions:

- docs/systems/theme-canary-contract.md — required labels (theme-canary
  + from-<consumer>), deterministic 12-hex sha1 dedupe key + hidden body
  marker, mandated open-AND-closed pre-filing search, 5-per-consumer-
  per-run cap, and the required evidence format (theme version/commit
  observed, page URL, rendered-vs-expected, minimal repro).
- .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/theme-canary.yml — issue form mirroring the
  evidence format, wired to the theme-canary label.
- docs/README.md — register the doc in the systems index.
- CHANGELOG.md — Unreleased entry.

Derived from both existing scouts, taking the stricter rule where they
differed; recording the observed theme version makes fixed-in-release
triage mechanical.

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): give the Dependabot label job an explicit GH_REPO (#370)
body:
The `label` job has been failing on every Dependabot PR since it was
added — `gh pr edit "$PR" --add-label auto-merge` exits 1 with
"fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git".

The job runs under `pull_request_target` and intentionally never checks
out the PR head, so `gh` has no git remote to infer the repository from.
auto-merge.yml already documents this gotcha for `gh pr diff` and
`gh pr merge`; this job hit the same wall without the workaround.

Setting GH_REPO points `gh` at the repository explicitly, with no
checkout. Because the label never landed, the `auto-merge` fast path
never engaged and every Dependabot PR sat open with a red check —
currently #354, #368 and #369.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: fix(giscus): comments were broken sitewide — add an end-to-end health check and correct the docs (#378)
body:
* feat(scripts): add `giscus-discussions doctor` to verify the comment chain

Every existing giscus check in this repo is static: the core test inspects
_config.yml keys and the include's Liquid, and the Playwright spec stubs
giscus.app out entirely. Both pass with a completely non-functional widget,
because the two things that actually break comments live on GitHub's side:

  1. the giscus GitHub App not being installed on the repository
  2. a data-repo-id / data-category-id belonging to a different repo (forks
     inherit the config but not the app installation)

`doctor` checks the whole chain end-to-end — repo public, Discussions enabled,
giscus.enabled, both IDs verified as actually belonging to this repo, and
finally the authoritative question only Giscus can answer: is the app
installed? Exits non-zero with a specific remediation line per failure.

Also fixes config key extraction: the existing helper only handled
data-category-id via a fragile nested-quote sed. Replaced with a block-scoped
awk that takes an arbitrary key and strips comments and quotes.

author: Amr
subject: fix(cookie-consent): text-dark on bg-body made privacy rights invisible in dark mode (#386)
body:
* fix(cookie-consent): text-dark on bg-body made privacy rights invisible in dark mode

The "Your Privacy Rights" list used Bootstrap's fixed `text-dark` utility
inside a `bg-body` panel. `.text-dark` resolves to `rgba(var(--bs-dark-rgb), 1)`
and `--bs-dark-rgb` is never remapped by `[data-bs-theme=dark]`, so it stays
`33,37,41` — byte-for-byte the dark `--bs-body-bg` (#212529). Measured in a
browser: 1.00:1 against WCAG 1.4.3 (AA)'s 4.5:1 minimum. The sibling <h6>
already used the mode-adaptive `text-body`; only the <ul> was hardcoded.

Also swaps `.cookie-category`'s hardcoded `#dee2e6` border for
`var(--bs-border-color)` — the identical colour in light mode, a visible one
in dark.

The regression test asserts the measured contrast ratio rather than calling
axe: the skin system paints `body.zer0-bg-body::after` with the active skin's
SVG, and axe refuses to resolve a background under a pseudo element, so it
reports every contrast check in the dialog as `incomplete` and returns zero
violations on the broken markup. An axe-only assertion would pass vacuously.

Closes #280

* test(evidence): before/after evidence for the dark-mode cookie modal fix

Generated against the live dev server: dark-mode contrast measured
1.00:1 before (text-dark on bg-body) and 11.85:1 after (text-body);
light mode unchanged at 15.43:1. The BEFORE state reverts exactly the
two declarations the fix changed, on the fixed build.

from the page's h2 straight to h5. Six other dialogs already used the correct
<h2 class="...-title h5">, so the theme contradicted itself half the time.
The .h5 utility reproduces the exact sizing, so this is semantics-only.

The seventh (_layouts/admin.html) is not in the issue's inventory: that grep
searched only _includes/, so a dialog defined in a layout was invisible to it.
Same defect, same theme chrome, one line.

The regression test asserts the dialog-title contract directly rather than
leaning on axe. axe's heading-order rule catches only 2 of the 6 reachable
dialogs, because it compares each heading to the previous one in DOM order:
search-modal and info-section emit their title as the FIRST heading in the
document, and stats/section-sidebar follow same-level headings. An axe-only
test would pass vacuously for four of them.

Closes #318

* test(evidence): before/after evidence for the dialog heading-level fix

Generated against the live dev server for all six live dialogs: the
heading walk a screen-reader user makes (h2 -> h5, skipping two levels)
becomes h2 -> h2, while the rendered header band is byte-identical in
every case (.h5 preserves the exact sizing). The BEFORE state reverts
exactly the diff in the live DOM.

author: Amr
subject: fix(ci): stop discarding good translations when one page fails (#388)
body:
`scripts/translate.rb` exits 1 when ANY page fails validation, and a
workflow `if:` with no status function carries an implicit `success()`.
Together those threw away 49 correct translations — ~21 minutes of paid
model inference — because one page failed validation (run 30477839691),
then re-spent it from scratch on the next run.

Gate the "Open PR with generated translations" and "Normalise generated
prose" steps on `!cancelled()` so the pages that succeeded are still
normalised and still land on the `chore/i18n-translations` PR. The run
still reports failure and the bad page still stays untranslated: no
`continue-on-error`, no rescue around the failing unit, and
`translate.rb`'s exit code is unchanged.

Normalisation needs the same gate as the PR step — without it a
partially-failed run would push unnormalised prose and turn the oneline
check red on the translation PR.

`!cancelled()` rather than `always()`: a cancelled run must push nothing.

Adds `test_partial_output_survives_failure` to the i18n suite, which
parses translate.yml and asserts both gates, the absence of
`continue-on-error`/`always()`, the unchanged exit code, and the
blast-radius guards (`add-paths`, stable branch).

subject: fix(scripts): correct consumer auditor, plugin contract, and JSON-LD scope (#400)
body:
* fix(scripts): repair consumer-audit correctness and stop leaking theme schema to consumers

Acts on the 2026-08 fleet harmonization audit (docs/systems/).

audit tooling:
- detect_consumer_mode() matched `^remote_theme:` with no tolerance for
  whitespace before the colon, so the column-aligned YAML that 6 of 9 fleet
  consumers use never matched and each was silently reported as gem mode —
  skipping the plugin checks with no warning that they were skipped. Also
  treats `remote_theme: false` as gem mode.
- --format json emitted a trailing comma per entry, so the array always closed
  on `},\n]}`; and the human log lines went to stdout, mixing into the payload.
  Entries are now separated correctly and logging moves to stderr under json,
  so output pipes straight into jq.
- audit-consumer ignored Jekyll's `source:`, auditing the repo root of a
  relocated site tree and reporting a falsely clean result. It now follows
  `source:` for the scan while reading config/overrides from the root.

plugin contract:
- The manifest demanded `_plugins/obsidian_links.rb` of every remote_theme
  consumer, contradicting obsidian.instructions.md, which documents it as
  opt-in and skipped under the github-pages gem. Pages builds in safe mode and
  loads no local plugins, so nothing shipped here is mandatory:
  required_plugin_paths is now empty and the plugin is optional. This cleared
  7 false MISSING_PLUGIN reports that the mode-detection fix had exposed.

author: Amr
subject: fix(layouts): stop emitting dead sub-topic anchors in section sidebars (#402)
body:
The section sidebar emitted `<a href="#{{ subcat | slugify }}">` for every
tag with at least one post, but the matching `<section id="...">` target is
only rendered inside the `magazine` branch of _layouts/section.html, and
there only for `sub_categories limit: 5`, and only when the tag still has a
post once the featured hero is excluded.

So the anchors were dead in two separate ways:

  * `grid` and `list` sections emitted one dead anchor per tag — neither
    branch renders any sub-topic id. `section_style` also defaults to
    `grid`, so this was the common case, not an edge case.
  * `magazine` sections emitted dead anchors for tags 6-15, because the
    sidebar iterated `limit: 15` while the layout rendered `limit: 5`.

A clean build of this repo's own demo site carried 64 of them. They are
invalid markup, a dead click for keyboard and screen-reader users, and they
left the sidebar's IntersectionObserver scrollspy permanently unable to
activate — while the include's header advertises "Smooth scroll to
sections" as a feature. Downstream, this is what turned lifehacker.dev's
main red: its /news/wire/ page is `section_style: grid`, and a dispatch
coining the tags `slop` and `writing` pushed its link check over the gate.

An anchor is now emitted only where a target provably exists: the include
takes `section_style` and builds `_linkable_subcats` by reproducing the
layout's own set. Every other style renders `<button data-filter>`, which
the layout's existing [data-filter] …

author: Amr
subject: feat(layouts): add cookbook collection with recipe scaling and unit conversion (#414)
body:
* feat(layouts): add cookbook collection with recipe scaling and unit conversion

Adds a `recipes` collection that renders structured front matter as a working
recipe page, plus the cookbook landing page that indexes it.

`layout: recipe` builds the fact bar (prep/cook/rest/total, yield, difficulty,
cuisine, oven), a grouped ingredient checklist, a numbered method with per-step
timings and temperatures, a baker's-percentage ratio table, a per-serving
nutrition panel, and one schema.org/Recipe JSON-LD block. `layout: cookbook`
groups recipes into course sections from _data/recipe_courses.yml.

assets/js/recipe-scaler.js layers scaling and US/metric conversion on top:
changing the yield rescales every quantity, and the unit switch rewrites
amounts, units and oven temperatures in place — including volume<->weight,
driven by the densities in _data/ingredient_densities.yml and overridable per
ingredient. It is strictly progressive enhancement: Jekyll renders every amount
exactly as authored and the control bar stays hidden until the script reveals
it, so the page is complete and correct with JavaScript disabled. Ratio
percentages are computed at build time for the same reason.

Twelve components make up the set, four of them value helpers shared by the
rest. Each namespaces its Liquid variables (`_rq_*`, `_rd_*`, …) because Liquid
`assign` writes to the global scope even inside an include — without that, a
helper called twice from one caller clobbers the caller's variables, which …

subject: fix(navigation): fit all nav items, full-bleed bar, language into Settings (#423)
body:
* fix(navigation): fit all nav items, full-bleed bar, language into Settings

The navbar sat inside a centred .container-xl, so the menubar track never
exceeded ~740px against the ~815px the theme's seven top-level items need.
Every label rendered ellipsized ("Quick S…", "N…", "Noteb…", "Ab…") from
1200px up, while the bar left up to 300px of dead margin on either side of
the screen; below ~1050px the menu collapsed to bare icons.

Four changes give the labels their room:

- The bar is .container-fluid with a fluid gutter and spans the full screen
  width; consumers can opt back into a cap with --zer0-navbar-max-width.
- The brand cluster is capped at 30cqi of the bar so a long title cannot
  starve the menubar (cqi, not %, which resolves against the content-sized
  grid track and collapses the title to zero).
- Label density degrades in three measured tiers instead of two: icon+label
  at >= 51rem of track, label-only at 41-50.99rem (icons dropped so the more
  informative half survives), icon-only below 41rem. Each boundary is the
  width the tier below it actually needs.
- The home-link icons wait for 86rem, where they no longer cost the menubar
  more than it can spare.

Result on the demo site: 0 truncated labels from 992px to 2560px, and the
bar inset a uniform 12px at every width.

Also fixes Settings opening behind the mobile nav menu. Both are
offcanvas-end panels at $zindex-offcanvas, and _navbar.scss lifts the fixed
header (which carries the nav menu) to 1046 while…
